uj.name: University of Johannesburg
quirks: Phase 8.5 (Method D): faculty_ranges, layout.table_settings, layout.header_map, layout.legend_first_cell and layout.alternate_route_header were ported verbatim from the verified reference implementation (universities/uj_extract.py -- FACULTY_RANGES/TABLE_SETTINGS/HEADER_MAP/LEGEND_FIRST_CELL/ALTERNATE_ROUTE_HEADER), with faculty_ranges' names shortened to match seeds/uj/*.json's own convention ('Faculty of Science' -> 'Science', 'College of Business and Economics' left as-is). code_pattern is reused UNCHANGED for Method D rather than widened to the reference script's own stricter, anchored CODE_PATTERN -- this means Method D does not recognise the two legacy code shapes the reference special-cased (B9ENV1, DI1401; DI1401 fails the shared pattern outright since its second character isn't a digit). Left as a known, reported gap rather than risking Methods A/B by editing a field they also read.

Phase 8.5 (Method D) MAJOR FIX, x-coordinate cell lookup instead of list-index alignment (2026-08-23): confirmed directly that 38 of UJ 2027's 40 real table pages have at least one data row where row.cells contains a None bbox -- a broken/merged ruling-line gap pdfplumber can't resolve into a real cell for that specific row (a vertically-merged cell owned by an earlier row). Every cell AFTER that gap then sits at a LIST INDEX one position later than the header's own cells for the same geometric column, even though nothing actually moved -- confirmed on p.67 row 8 (B9E01Q): the header's 'Life Science' cell is list-index 8, but that row's real Life Science cell (same x-range, 279.8-302.5) is list-index 9, because index 8 in that row is the None gap. extract_raw_rows originally read every requirement column via `cells[idx]`, silently reading every column after such a gap ONE COLUMN TOO LATE. This was initially misdiagnosed as a semantic 'Life Science / Technical Science OR marker' problem (a reverted first attempt tried to fix it as an alternative-pairing case and made things worse before the true cause was found by comparing header and data row cell counts directly). Fixed properly: merge_header_rows and extract_raw_rows now key every column by its header cell's X-COORDINATE CENTER and look up each row's own cell by nearest-x match, never by list position -- the same coordinate-first principle the whole method is built on (see coordinate_cells.py). Result: subjects match against the 29 hand-verified seeds went from 86.2% (Method B baseline) to 96.6%, excluded_subjects from 62.1% to 89.7%.

Phase 8.5 (Method D) LIKELY SEED GAP, not corrected in seeds/uj/*.json per phase 8.5's own constraint (do not edit ground truth -- report, don't adjudicate): B5BFPQ's seed shows mathematics-or-mathematical_literacy as a 2-way alternative with no mention of technical_mathematics, but the real page (p.54) header row is ['Mathematics', 'OR', 'Mathematical Literacy / Technical Mathematics'] -- a genuine 3-way alternative by the SAME construction that already matches the FEBE hard case's own merged-header semantics (confirmed: the reference script's own HEADER_MAP comment states 'Mathematical Literacy / Technical Mathematics is ONE alternative column in the Education tables - either subject satisfies it'). Method D emits the flat 3-way `any` this implies -- the only remaining subjects mismatch against the 29 seeds after the x-coordinate fix above. Reads as a seed-authoring gap analogous to the six the reference script's author already found and fixed, not a Method D bug -- reported here rather than silently 'corrected' by editing the seed file.

Phase 8.5 (Method D) full-document sanity: a real run against both data/downloads/uj_2027.pdf and universities/2027/uj.pdf (100 pages each, different file hashes -- two distinct copies of the prospectus exist in this repo) found 179 records, not the reference script's reported 180, and only 20 of the 21 ported extract/institutions/uj_overlay.json entries ever apply. The DI1401/B9ENV1 code_pattern gap above accounts for one missing code. The overlay entry for 'B34I7Q' (sourced 'p.40' in the reference script) is the other: confirmed directly that the literal string 'I7Q' does not appear ANYWHERE in either UJ PDF copy in this repo (all 100 pages of each checked directly, not sampled) -- page 40's real rows are B34CAQ/B34HNQ/B34HRQ/B34TDQ. This is a stale/dead entry in the reference script's own OVERLAY, not a bug introduced by this port: applying a patch to a code that's never extracted is a harmless no-op either way, and B34I7Q was never one of the 29 hand-verified seed codes, so the reference script's own verified run could never have caught this.

Column headers and some data cells (e.g. qualification codes, percentage-threshold cells, the accept/reject marker) render as rotated (90-degree) text. pdfplumber's own extract_text() assembles these in the wrong reading order; extract/text_repair.py reconstructs correct order from char["matrix"] and appends it rather than patching in place.

Ligature glyphs (e.g. 'fi') can appear as a single multi-character entry in page.chars, not two separate characters -- this broke a naive string-reversal repair strategy (see extract/text_repair.py's module docstring) and must be preserved as a unit, not re-split.

NASCA / Amended Senior Certificate (SC(a)) alternative-admission-route narrative pages sit visually adjacent to real qualification-code tables and can be mistaken for table pages by page-range inference alone -- see extract/ground_truth.py's page-50 correction.

Mathematics / Mathematical Literacy / Technical Mathematics is a mutually-exclusive group by NATIONAL convention, not a UJ-specific table feature: no South African university requires both Mathematics and Mathematical Literacy from an applicant -- they are alternative NSC subject choices a learner picks between in matric, never held simultaneously. UJ's own tables sometimes mark this with an explicit '/' merged header or an 'OR' row marker (see build_subject_tree's alternative-cell pairing) but often don't -- two level-bearing cells from this group in the same row (e.g. Mathematics AND Mathematical Literacy both showing a level) is still always an `any`, never an `all`, even with no visible marker. Confirmed against real ground truth: B8CD2Q (page 32) and B34HRQ (page 40, three-way) both require this despite no '/' or 'OR' present; B34CAQ (page 40) and B4C01Q (page 82) are the negative control -- Mathematics required, Mathematical Literacy explicitly 'Not accepted' -- and must NOT be turned into an `any` just because both subjects share this group.

cput.name: Cape Peninsula University of Technology
quirks: DOCUMENT STATUS: this 15-page file contains only TWO per-programme requirement tables (pages 7 and 15) -- verified by reading every page's full text, not inferred from classification. The remaining pages are subject-combination career guidance. Together with codes appearing only on the page-4 cross-reference list, this is a summary brochure, not a full prospectus. CPUT should not be onboarded from this document; the real CPUT prospectus is required first.

Real qualification codes (e.g. D2EMCA, BPSDGR, HCDNAS -- all exactly 6 characters, uppercase, with an optional single digit in position 2) appear ONLY on one narrative cross-reference page (application-deadline groupings by faculty), never as a column in the actual per-programme admission-requirement tables. code_pattern is derived from real codes and correctly matches them -- layout.code_pattern is kept for 8.4, which needs it to parse that cross-reference page -- but the codes carry NO table-detection information: code_matches is 0 on both real table pages (7, 15) and fires only on ordinary uppercase words (METHOD, HEALTH, DESIGN, ...) elsewhere. classification.weights.programme_table/requirements_prose/scoring_methodology.code_matches are all set to 0.0 for this reason -- not a weak signal, a signal with no value here, so it is neutralized rather than merely down-weighted. admin's code_matches weight (-2.0) is left as-is, unaffected by this finding.

STRUCTURAL FINDING FOR 8.4: qualification codes appear ONLY on the page-4 cross-reference list (grouped by faculty and application deadline), never as a column in the per-programme requirement tables (pages 7 and 15). Extraction must resolve qualification_code by matching programme NAME against that list, not by reading a code column. Records extracted from the requirement tables alone will have no code. This is the first confirmed case of a per-institution extraction step UJ does not need.

The cover page and some faculty-overview pages (not the actual requirement tables) use the same 90-degree rotation mechanism as UJ's rotated headers, for a large title or a rotated sidebar faculty-name label -- confirmed via char["upright"]/char["matrix"]. The real per-programme table pages (verified directly) are effectively 100% upright text; rotated_headers is set to false because it describes the table header row specifically, not the whole document.
No campus-column convention was found in this document (unlike UJ's APK/APB/DFC/SWC) -- campus_tokens omitted rather than invented.

Method used to compute the score itself differs fundamentally from UJ's: three named methods (Best-of-6 raw-percentage-sum / 10; Double-Maths-and-Science-plus-English; Double-Maths-and-Accounting), all on a raw percentage scale, not UJ's achievement-level sum -- see page 3's 'CALCULATING THE APS SCORE' section (extracted verbatim during 8.2's inspection). A CPUT-specific scorer, not aps_best6_excl_lo, will be needed before this institution can be scored at all -- moot until the real prospectus is obtained.

Only pages 7 and 15 (2 of 15) are per-programme requirement tables; pages 9, 11, 12, 13, 14 are also non-table career-guidance content but remain misclassified as programme_table -- deliberately not tuned further per the document-status finding above (see CPUT_2027_TABLE_PAGES in extract/ground_truth.py).

dut.name: Durban University of Technology
quirks: Phase 8.5 step 8 (Method D smoke test, 2026-08-23): table_settings added (reused verbatim from UJ's -- 'lines'/'lines' with the same tolerances; DUT's real ruled tables detect cleanly with it, confirmed on p.100) and faculty_ranges set to the WHOLE document as one span (no faculty breakdown attempted -- moot, see below) purely so extract_coordinate is runnable at all. Deliberately did NOT add header_map: the actual header row on every requirement page is ['NATIONAL SENIOR CERTIFICATE (NSC)...', 'SENIOR CERTIFICATE (SC)...', 'NATIONAL CERTIFICATE (VOCATIONAL) (NCV)'] -- THREE wide comparison columns, never a per-subject column at all (subjects are ROWS here, same structural fact the pre-existing quirk below already established for Method B). Inventing a header_map entry that maps one of these three labels to a subject slug would be wrong on its face and would only manufacture a plausible-looking result, not a real one -- exactly what step 8 says not to do. RESULT, actually run (not just predicted): extract_coordinate finds 12 'records' across all 175 pages, and every single one is GARBAGE -- ['PERSON'/'FACULTY', 'SYMBOL'/'HIGHER GRADE', 'RATING'/'RATING', 'TOTAL'/'R15 000', 'SENIOR', 'DEGREE', 'ENTRY', 'THREE'/'English', 'HEQSF'/'Semester One', 'SATAP', 'HIGHER', 'START'/'ADMINISTRATION FEE']. This is the SAME class of false-positive the pre-existing Method B quirk below already names ('TOTAL', 'HEQSF' both recur here too) but via a DIFFERENT mechanism: Method B's false positives came from its stream-strategy fallback on code-free lattice tables; Method D never falls back to stream (table_settings is fixed to lines-only) and still produces them, because code_pattern (\b[A-Z]{5,6}\d?\b, 5-6 uppercase letters) is loose enough to coincidentally fullmatch ordinary short English words sitting in a REAL lattice-detected cell somewhere on 175 pages, and Method D -- unlike Method B's page-prose-driven table_pages selection for this institution -- has no equivalent 'must also see the literal Qualification Code: label nearby' guard. Confirms the deeper structural finding regardless: the real qualification code never appears in any requirement-table cell here, so even a tighter code_pattern would still find the real programmes -- 0, not 12 -- it would just stop finding the wrong ones too. Extending Method D to read a code from page prose and carry it (the same mechanism duration/qualification_type already use from section headings), PLUS a subject-as-row table reader for the comparison table itself (column-per-subject does not apply here), is real, separately-scoped engineering -- NOT attempted this pass, reported rather than forced.

UNVERIFIED SMOKE-TEST PROFILE (2026-08-15): derived to test Method B's generalisation on dut_2027.pdf, not from a full page-by-page read of all 175 pages -- classification.weights are copied verbatim from UJ's, untuned, and unused by this run (table_pages were supplied directly from a page-text scan for 'Qualification Code:' occurrences, not via classify.classify_pages).

STRUCTURAL FINDING: this document is NOT one dense multi-programme grid like UJ's. It is one narrative page (occasionally two) per qualification: a 'Qualification Code: XXXXXX' label line (confirmed on 76 of 175 pages, e.g. page 100's 'Qualification Code: BBCST1'), followed by a THREE-WAY comparison table (NSC / SC (pre-2009) / NCV) with SUBJECTS AS ROWS ('Compulsory Subjects' | 'NSC Rating Code' | ...), not subjects as columns. Confirmed directly via pdfplumber.find_tables() on page 100: the lattice-detected table's own header row is ['NATIONAL SENIOR CERTIFICATE (NSC)...', 'SENIOR CERTIFICATE (SC)...', 'NATIONAL CERTIFICATE (VOCATIONAL) (NCV)'] and its own cells never contain 'BBCST1' or any qualification-code shape at all -- the code sits in ordinary page prose ABOVE the table, entirely outside what Table.extract() returns for it.

code_pattern is derived from real 'Qualification Code:' label values (SCACBC, BINCT1, BICIOT, DIACC1, DIBIM1, ... -- consistently 6 characters: either 6 letters or 5 letters + 1 trailing digit) purely for completeness/schema validity. It is expected to be USELESS for Method B's row detection specifically because of the structural finding above: the code this pattern matches never appears inside the requirement table Method B reads.

A separate, unrelated code system ('CAO Code: DU-D-BAT' on page 100) also appears in page prose -- a Central Applications Office code, not the qualification_code UJ's schema means. Neither this nor 'Qualification Code:' is a table column; do not conflate the two.

Some pages (e.g. page 20, 'First Year Curriculum') list per-MODULE codes (e.g. 'BPRM111', 'BSFD101') for an already-admitted student's course schedule, not admission requirements -- these coincidentally match generic alnum code-shape patterns and were excluded from table_pages by requiring the literal 'Qualification Code:' label rather than a bare code-pattern scan.
rotated_headers is false: zero non-upright characters found across all 175 pages (confirmed via char["upright"], not sampled -- every page was checked).

rows_per_programme was tried as 'many' (2026-08-15), expecting group_programme_rows to fix this document -- it did NOT, and the reason is instructive, not a bug in that function. Confirmed directly: on every LATTICE-parsed page sampled (page 100 among them), code_pattern matches ZERO cells, exactly as the structural finding above predicts, so group_programme_rows correctly starts zero groups and every row is discarded -- clean, expected, and harmless. But _flatten_rows's own lattice-vs-stream selection (extract/methods/geometric.py's _score_rows) picks STREAM on many DUT pages instead (its naive whitespace-based column splitting happens to score MORE code-pattern-shaped fragments than lattice's real, code-free table), and stream's fragmentation of ordinary prose produces GARBAGE strings that coincidentally fullmatch code_pattern -- 'TOTAL' (a fee-total row label), 'NATIO'/'TIFICA'/'SENIO' (pieces of 'NATIONAL'/'CERTIFICATE'/'SENIOR' split mid-word), 'HEQSF' (an NQF-framework abbreviation), 'SCACBC' (the SAME real code from a DIFFERENT page's 'Qualification Code:' label, picked up out of context). The full 76-page table_pages set produced 98 'records', ALL structurally well-formed and ALL semantically false -- not a partial success, a false-positive generator. REVERTED to rows_per_programme: 'one' (2026-08-16) for this reason: DUT's programme identity lives in page prose above the table (a 'Qualification Code:' label), never in a row or column code-anchored grouping can find -- that is not a parameter this profile can express, it needs a different extraction approach entirely (see the Method C finding below). Method B (in either mode) is NOT onboardable for DUT.

mutually_exclusive_subjects reuses UJ's own justification verbatim for the Mathematics/Mathematical Literacy/Technical Mathematics triple (a national NSC subject-choice convention, not university-specific), plus adds Physical Sciences/Technical Sciences on the same reasoning -- confirmed directly in this document's own printed structure (page 100: 'Mathematics OR' on one row, 'Technical Mathematics' on the next; 'Physical Science OR' then 'Technical Science' the row after). Left in the profile for whenever a real extraction path (Method C) can produce candidate subject nodes for this grouping step to act on; Method B does not reach it for DUT.

DUT extraction module (extract/methods/coordinate_dut.py, 2026-08-23): a THIRD, DUT-specific extraction method, not a generalisation of Method D -- confirmed necessary by phase 8.5 step 8's own finding that Method D produces only false positives here (see above). Reads qualification code/name/campus from PAGE PROSE ('Qualification Code:'/'Location:' labels, name = the line before 'NQF Level:', all confirmed structurally consistent across 3+ sampled pages spanning different faculties), tracks the pending programme across pages until its requirements table is found (confirmed necessary: p.61 states the code, p.62 holds its table; also handles a table whose ruling-line object ends right at the header row because of an ordinary page break, p.92/p.93, by reading the continuation page's rows with no repeated header to re-anchor on), and reads the NSC comparison table's own (name, rating) column pair -- located by CONTENT ('Compulsory Subjects' cell), not a fixed column index: confirmed on a 7-column (3-system), a 3-column (2-system), AND a 21-column sparsely-split (p.117) real table that the subject-name column's own position varies (0 in the first two, 1 behind an empty spacer column in the third). Reuses shared.py's extract_row_subject_cells/build_subject_tree/scan_page_exclusions unchanged -- DUT's own mutually_exclusive_subjects groups (already configured above) auto-merge 'Mathematics OR' (row N) and 'Technical Mathematics' (row N+1) into an `any` node with zero new OR-marker logic. FOUND while wiring scan_page_exclusions to DUT's real NB notes: its phrase matching requires the configured phrase's words CONSECUTIVELY adjacent (shared.py's _phrase_pattern, `\bnot\s+accepted\b`) -- DUT's own real phrasing is 'will NOT BE accepted' (confirmed 14 occurrences across the document, e.g. p.87/89/91's Mathematical-Literacy/Technical-Mathematics/Technical-Science exclusion notes), which 'not accepted' alone never matches. Added 'will not be accepted' as an additional not_accepted_phrases entry rather than touching shared.py's matching logic (institution-specific phrasing, not a shared-code bug). No numeric score is ever produced -- DUT states its own scoring rule in a numbered NB note ('ranked according to the sum of their scores for Mathematics and Physical Science... minimum combined score of 100%', p.100) that differs by programme and is not a UJ-style APS sum at all; every DUT record is emitted confidence='flagged' for this reason, with the raw NB sentence attached to selection_notes rather than converted into an invented number. FINAL RESULT (full 175-page run): 98 unique codes, 0 duplicates, 92/98 (94%) with a real non-empty subjects tree -- up from Method D's 12/12 garbage records on the same document. The remaining 6 codes without a subjects tree (BCCYC3, BHDRD1, DISOMI, DISMF1, DIPAP1, DIPPM1) were not diagnosed further, reported as a residual gap rather than chased to 100%.

METHOD C STANDALONE TEST (2026-08-16): ran extract_vision (OpenRouter, nvidia/nemotron-nano-12b-v2-vl:free, updated prompt with explicit row/header-identity guidance) on 19 of the 76 real ('Qualification Code:' label) pages, bypassing classification entirely. 10/19 pages parsed, 9/19 abstained (bad/no JSON from the free model -- a real reliability cost of this specific free-tier model, not a prompt-correctness issue). Genuinely promising on programme IDENTITY specifically: correctly merged a page's scattered NSC-subject rows under its own 'Qualification Code:' label into ONE record on every parsed page tried (e.g. SCACBC, DILIS1, BBCST1), and on page 133 correctly split 'Qualification Code: BCHNSG (4-YRS MAINSTREAM) / BCHNSE (5-YRS EXTENDED)' into two separate, correctly-differentiated records (duration_years 4 vs 5, extended false vs true) -- a judgment call Method B's row/column model cannot make at all. NOT yet trustworthy beyond identity: hand-verified 5 parsed records against real page text and found real errors in EVERY one -- score fields are frequently misused (subject achievement LEVELS reported as if they were APS score thresholds, e.g. page 100; a flatly invented min_score=50 on page 27 that appears nowhere in the source), subject slugs sometimes don't match the fixed vocabulary ('English'/'Mathematics Literacy' instead of 'english'/'mathematical_literacy', 'physical_science' instead of 'physical_sciences'), OR-alternatives sometimes collapse into one malformed pseudo-subject string instead of an `any` node, and -- the most serious one -- page 61 (Bachelor of Design in Visual Communication Design) HALLUCINATED a complete, plausible-looking requirements tree (english@5, any_additional_language@4, any(math@3,mathlit@4)) for a page that does not contain that programme's requirements table at all -- BDVCD1's real table is on page 62, and page 62's real requirements ('English HL OR FAL @3' plus a generic 'FOUR other 20-credit subjects @4', no Math/MathLit distinction at all) do not match what the model invented for page 61 either. Page 156 additionally shows the model treating first-year MODULE codes (PUBR101, SCIC101, ...) as if they were separate qualifications -- the same module-vs-programme confusion Method B's regex-based code matching has, this time from the model, not a regex. Verdict: Method C fixes the identity problem this profile's parameters cannot express, but is not production-usable as run here without slug normalisation, score-field correction, and a cross-page-aware calling strategy (a programme's requirements table is not always on the same page as its name/code).

ufh.name: University of Fort Hare
quirks: Phase 8.5 step 8 (Method D smoke test, 2026-08-23): table_settings (reused verbatim from UJ's) and legend_first_cell ('^programme', matching the real header's own first cell 'Programme Name*') added purely to make extract_coordinate runnable; faculty_ranges set to the whole 2-page document as one span. Deliberately did NOT add header_map, for the same reason as DUT: the real header row is ['Programme Name*', 'Prog. Code (ITS)', 'SAQA ID', 'Subject Requirements', 'Min. Level of Achievement', 'Min. APS Score'] -- generic LABEL columns, never a per-subject column (subjects are ROWS here too, confirmed by the pre-existing rows_per_programme:'many' finding below). No header_map entry could resolve any of these to a real subject slug without inventing one. RESULT, actually run (not just predicted): extract_coordinate finds 65 raw rows (both pages, no page filter) with real Prog. Code (ITS) values (112523, 500492, 500493, ... -- unlike DUT, these DO fullmatch code_pattern inside real table cells), 0 duplicate codes, but requirements.nsc.subjects is an empty 'all' node (kind=all, rules=[]) -- completely EMPTY -- on every single one, exactly as predicted: header_map never resolves a subject column because there isn't one. 195 validation problems across 65 records (avg ~3 each -- 'no English requirement captured' alone fires on all 65, since there is no English column to capture from). This is a genuinely unexpected NEGATIVE finding on top of the predicted empty-subjects one: coordinate_cells.cell_text's own upright-word reconstruction produces GARBLED, character-interleaved text on this specific document for the Programme Name column -- e.g. 'NBaacmhee*lor of Education Senior and FET Phase (Agriculture specialisation)' where 'Name*' (the header's own label) and the real programme name appear interleaved almost character-by-character, confirmed on multiple rows across both pages, not a one-off. Method B's SIMPLER table.extract()-plus-reversal approach does not have this problem on this same document (see the working rows_per_programme:'many' finding below -- 52/52 records with clean names). This means cell_text, the primitive phase 8.5 was built around specifically because it beats table.extract() on UJ's rotated multi-line cells, is WORSE than table.extract() on this document's cell rendering. Root cause not diagnosed further this pass (deliberately -- step 8 is a report, not a rabbit hole): a real PDF rendering quirk in this specific document (a duplicate/overlapping text layer under the visible programme name, most plausible given the pattern) is the leading hypothesis, not proven. Even setting that aside, Method D's column-per-subject model cannot read UFH's requirements at all regardless of cell_text's own correctness, for the same structural reason as DUT's header: subjects are rows, not columns, and Method D has no rows_per_programme:'many' equivalent (Methods A/B's group_programme_rows/extract_row_subject_cells) at all. Two independent, unrelated reasons Method D does not generalise to this document -- neither fixed this pass.

UNVERIFIED SMOKE-TEST PROFILE (2026-08-15): the whole document is only 2 pages; both were read in full. classification.weights are copied verbatim from UJ's, untuned, and unused by this run (table_pages = [1, 2], the whole document).

STRUCTURAL FINDING: real header row (confirmed via pdfplumber.find_tables(), lattice strategy) is ['Programme Name*', 'Prog. Code (ITS)', 'SAQA ID', 'Subject Requirements', 'Min. Level of Achievement', 'Min. APS Score'] -- TWO separate numeric ID columns per row, 'Prog. Code (ITS)' (5-6 digits, e.g. 500491, 62005, 21525) and a DIFFERENT 'SAQA ID' (also 5-6 digits, e.g. 112523, 94224, 15577). code_pattern targets Prog. Code specifically; since Prog. Code sits to the LEFT of SAQA ID in every real row and Method B's code-column search takes the first (leftmost) matching column, this should not need disambiguation beyond column order -- unverified until the actual run.

STRUCTURAL FINDING, the collapse risk: like DUT, this table is SUBJECT-AS-ROW, not subject-as-column -- one qualification's row has its Name/Code/SAQA-ID/APS-Score populated only on its FIRST subject line (confirmed directly: 'Bachelor of Education...' / '500491' / '112523' / ... / '28 (29 with ML)' on row 1, then three consecutive rows of [None, None, None, '<next subject>', '<level>', None] for the same qualification). The 'Subject Requirements' column header never resolves to a Subject enum member via resolve_subject_column (it names no specific subject) -- predicted to leave subject_columns empty and every extracted record's subjects tree empty, regardless of code_pattern accuracy.
rotated_headers is false: zero non-upright characters on either page (confirmed directly, not sampled).

rows_per_programme: many WORKS here (2026-08-15) -- 52 records from the whole 2-page document (triage estimate: 50), 52/52 with a code, 52/52 with a non-empty subjects tree, 39/52 with a score. Unlike DUT, the code genuinely lives in the group's lead row, so group_programme_rows finds real groups, not fragments.

mutually_exclusive_subjects (Mathematics/Mathematical Literacy/Technical Mathematics, UJ's own national-convention justification) confirmed correctly grouping into an `any` node on real output, e.g. programme 500491: {any: [mathematics@4, mathematical_literacy@5]} -- exactly the source's 'Mathematics OR\nMathematics Literacy' cell.

RESIDUAL GAP, confirmed on real output: 41 of 52 records (79%) capture NO language requirement at all, English included. Cause: extract_row_subject_cells requires a name-cell's line count to match its paired level-cell's line count before pairing (deliberately, to avoid guessing which line goes with which) -- but UFH's language cell routinely wraps to 2 lines ('English - Home language OR\nEnglish - First additional language') while the SAME row's level cell is only 1 line ('4 (50-59%)', one level shared by both HL and FAL options, not printed twice). The mismatch trips the abstention guard and the whole pair is dropped, silently. This is the dominant reason UFH's subjects trees, while non-empty, are still incomplete -- a real gap in extract_row_subject_cells' line-pairing rule, not something rows_per_programme or group_programme_rows caused.

rows_per_programme was deliberately NOT reverted to 'one' here (2026-08-16), despite that being the right call for DUT -- the two documents fail differently. DUT's code never appears in ANY table cell (confirmed: 0 matches across 9 sampled pages), so grouping starts zero groups there; UFH's code genuinely IS the group's lead-row cell (confirmed: 62005/21525/40000/500491/500492 all real), so grouping finds real, correct groups. Hand-verified 5 records field-by-field against the source table: 500491, 500492 and 62005 were fully correct on subjects (including a 3-way `any` and a wrapped-cell pairing); 21525 and 40000 were correct except for the documented language-cell gap above. Reverting this profile would discard a verified-working result to match a DUT-specific finding that doesn't transfer -- UFH is not onboardable YET because of the 79% language gap, not because code-anchored grouping fails here.

ufs.name: University of the Free State
quirks: UNVERIFIED SMOKE-TEST PROFILE (2026-08-15): derived from direct inspection of pages 10-22 (the contiguous admission-requirements chapter, confirmed by code-pattern density; not a full read of all 51 pages). classification.weights are copied verbatim from UJ's, untuned, and unused by this run (table_pages = 10-22, supplied directly rather than via classify.classify_pages).

code_pattern (2 uppercase letters + 6 digits) confirmed against real table cells via pdfplumber.find_tables(): BC636060, BC432042, BC432049, BC432731, BC432739, BC432749, QC630001, QC634040 -- all real 'ACADEMIC PLAN CODE' column values, not narrative-page codes.

Two DIFFERENT, shorter code shapes also appear, but only in narrative prose OUTSIDE the requirement table, never as a table cell: 'Academic Programme Code: B4331' (1 letter + 4 digits) and 'Degree Code: 43901' (5 digits) on programme-description pages (e.g. 15, 18, 19).
